response: Yes, many patients in regional and rural Australia are willing participants in community-based medical education. In fact, studies have shown that patients in these areas often appreciate the opportunity to contribute to the education of future healthcare professionals and are generally supportive of medical students and junior doctors being involved in their care. This willingness to participate can be attributed to the strong sense of community and social responsibility that exists in many rural and regional areas, as well as a recognition of the importance of training the next generation of healthcare professionals to address workforce shortages in these regions.
